findings.note: The new export guard is fail-open one level below the top, while its header presents itself as the enforcement of Spec 3 section 5's fail-closed export. reflect.VisibleFields(reflect.TypeOf(run.Snapshot{})) enumerates only Snapshot's own fields, so a field added to any type Snapshot reaches through - GateError, Finding, Bug, Golden, AllowedCmd, BugStatus, TokenTotals - is never classified and is exported verbatim. GateError is exactly the type whose Detail is blanked because it can carry cmd stdout/stderr, and the export's default destination is <RepoRoot>/docs/metareview/fsm/<run-id>/, which CLAUDE.md instructs the operator to commit. The same gap applies to the event() path, which likewise blanks only error.detail. Either walk nested struct types (recursing on struct/pointer-to-struct/slice-of-struct fields reachable from Snapshot) or narrow the header comment so it does not claim more than the assertion delivers.

findings.note: One classification note in the verbatim map misdescribes its own field. "mock": "flag" is wrong: run.Snapshot.Mock is a string, not a bool, and it holds "<repo-relative mock dir>#<sha256[:16]>" (internal/fsm/machine/machine.go:175). Exporting it verbatim is still the right call - the fork spec section 5 explicitly notes 'init.mock is already repo-relative' - but the map is precisely the decision record this test exists to force an author to write, so a note that gets the value's shape wrong defeats its purpose for the next reader deciding whether the neighbouring path-shaped fields need the same treatment. "flag" is correct for calibration and mock_tainted, which are real bools.

findings.note: CLAUDE.md's new Durable Output sentence 'A `mock: true` FSM row never satisfies a gate.' reads as an enforced invariant but no code enforces it. grep across internal/epicready, internal/prready, internal/taskdone, internal/artifactreview, internal/state and internal/runchain finds no reference to mock at all; record.Row.Mock (internal/fsm/record/record.go:44) is written and never read by any gate, and runchain.Resolve matches on scope and target only. It holds today only because FSM rows carry scope "fsm-<workflow>" and target type "fsm", so they structurally never match a task-done/epic-ready/pr-ready chain - not because anything checks the flag. The fsm-cli spec itself lists this beside 'never pass a secret via --var' as a documented caveat and internal/fsm/cli/prompt.go:46 states it as operator guidance, so the surrounding intent is policy. Phrasing it in CLAUDE.md as a property invites a reader to rely on an enforcement that is not there; either word it as policy or add the check.
